drills.q: Why 3f+1 replicas for f Byzantine faults? Show the quorum-intersection argument.
drills.a: Quorums of size 2f+1 among N=3f+1: any two intersect in >=2(2f+1)-3f+1... compute: |A n B| = |A|+|B|-N = (4f+2)-(3f+1) = f+1, so at least one HONEST node sits in both. Two conflicting commits would each need an honest member to sign both - impossible.

drills.q: Name all three Ethereum slashing conditions and the penalty curve.
drills.a: 1) Double proposal: two headers signed for same slot. 2) Double vote: conflicting attestations for same target epoch. 3) Surround vote: attestations with illegally nested source/target ranges. Penalty: initial slash 1/32 of effective balance (<=1 ETH), then correlation penalty ~min(3 * fraction_slashed_within_4096_epochs, 1) * balance - solo ~1 ETH, coordinated mass events -> total loss.

drills.q: What is weak subjectivity and why must PoS accept it?
drills.a: New/returning nodes cannot distinguish canonical chain from an attacker's long-range fabricated history (no cumulative work metric exists). Mitigation: trust a recent state root from the live network. Accepted because fabricating requires majority stake colluding publicly and self-slashing.

drills.q: Compare PBFT vs HotStuff on message complexity and why it mattered for production chains.
drills.a: PBFT: every replica broadcasts to everyone, O(n^2) per phase, quadratic view-change - dead beyond ~100 validators. HotStuff: votes go only to leader who aggregates threshold-signed QCs, O(n) per view, linear view change, pipelined 3-chain commit. This is what let Diem/Aptos/Sui-class chains run hundreds of validators at sub-second finality.

drills.q: Finality stalls but blocks keep being produced on Ethereum. What happened in May 2023 and how do you monitor for it?
drills.a: Client bugs (Prysm, then Teku) split attestation weights so no checkpoint reached 2/3 - finality froze ~25 min and again ~60+ min while blocks continued. Monitor justification-gap alarms (epochs since last finality), not block height; prevent via client diversity targets (no client >1/3 of stake).

drills.q: Explain the inactivity leak and its CAP-style tradeoff.
drills.a: If >1/3 of stake is offline >4 epochs, finality can never resume; leak drains offline balances quadratically until online remainder holds 2/3 and finalizes. Chooses availability over frozen consistency, paid by the absent minority. Rejoining side syncs forward; no reconciliation with its stale history.

drills.q: Design consensus for 12 banks settling tokenized deposits. Pick the family and defend against 'just use a database'.
drills.a: BFT family (HotStuff/QBFT/Tendermint lineage): bounded known membership, N=13 tolerates f=3, second-level deterministic finality fits settlement, no token needed (legal/reputational bonds substitute). Database wins if settlement truth never leaves one operator; blockchain earns its seat when counterparties need shared verifiable settlement without a designated operator.

drills.q: An L2 advertises soft confirmations in 200 ms. Decompose what that guarantee actually is.
drills.a: One operator's local ordering promise - not consensus. Ladder: soft confirm (sequencer) -> batch posted to L1 blobs (data available, reorderable until finality) -> L1 finalization (~12.8 min). Risks: sequencer equivocation, forced-inclusion delays. Use for UX; gate irreversible actions on finalized state or priced preconfirmation markets.

drills.q: Why does BLS aggregation matter more than TPS for Ethereum's architecture?
drills.a: ~10^6 validator units cannot broadcast individual signatures: committees attest per slot and BLS collapses thousands of sigs into one ~96-byte aggregate, making GHOST weighting by millions of votes and FFG checkpoints fit home-node bandwidth. Costs: slower verification than ECDSA, rogue-key defenses needed (deposit proofs-of-possession).

drills.q: Quantify Bitcoin's daily security budget and name its structural fragility.
drills.a: Subsidy 3.125 BTC/block post-April-2024 halving ~450 BTC/day plus fees; miners recoup via hardware+energy so attack means outbidding that flow or buying majority ASIC capacity unavailable on rental markets. Fragility: subsidy halves every 4 years while fee share remains volatile - long-run fee-only security is unresolved.

drills.q: Where do rollups sit in the trilemma? State precisely what they rent.
drills.a: They rent decentralization+security from L1 (data availability via blobs, settlement) and buy scalability through compressed execution off-chain; their own sequencer is currently centralized - the honest weak point until shared/decentralized sequencing ships. Trilemma relocated, not solved: L1 blob bandwidth is the global bottleneck.

drills.q: If a deposit is denominated in a smaller-cap PoW altcoin instead of Bitcoin, should you use Bitcoin's confirmation policy?
drills.a: No. Smaller-cap chains have dramatically less total hashrate, so the same nominal 'q=0.3 attacker' is achievable at far lower absolute cost -- real, documented 51% attacks against smaller chains have used rented hashpower from public marketplaces. Confirmation policy must be set per-chain based on its actual current hashrate and rentable-hashpower cost.
